This issue is currently awaiting triage.

If a SIG or subproject determines this is a relevant issue, they will accept it by applying the `triage/accepted` label and provide further guidance.

The `triage/accepted` label can be added by org members by writing `/triage accepted` in a comment.


<details>

Instructions for interacting with me using PR comments are available [here](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md).  If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [kubernetes-sigs/prow](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/prow/issues/new?title=Prow%20issue:) repository.
</details>

There are other locations in the code base where `Event` should be used, but where format characters are not present:
 * Eg: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3f3fdc1aa62002a58bec1141fe69e86bbb27491/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/reconciler/reconciler.go#L394

Thank you for pointing out the issue, unexpected formatting problems might arise when error messages are treated as format strings rather than string literals.
And it is essential to fix this issue; as CSI drivers produce errors with special characters.
The potential fix to this issue is to replace the `Eventf` call with `Event` to treat the error message as a string literal.
use a format string like `"%s"` explicitly to safely handle the error message.

> There are other locations in the code base

I believe we should fix all the locations where `Eventf` is used.
I am interested to work on this and will raise a PR for the same

> I believe we should fix all the locations where `Eventf` is used.

Agreed.

> I am interested to work on this and will raise a PR for the same

@Shilpa-Gokul Thanks! If you can audit other `Eventf` calls for volume/storage, that would be appreciated as well (anywhere that `Eventf` is called with only 4 parameters is suspect).
